```{r}
# Wilson interval for a binomial proportion.
wilson <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) {
  p <- x / n
  d <- 1 + z^2 / n
  c <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / d
  h <- (z / d) * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  c(lo = pmax(0, c - h), hi = pmin(1, c + h))
}
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-24. Draft classes
after the last complete draft are administratively right-censored and carry
no outcomes, so they are excluded from every rate below rather than counted
as failures.*
:::

## 1. Introduction

The modeling objective of this project includes setting the dependent variable or outcome: whether a college player is drafted, whether he reaches the NFL by any route, and whether he plays once he arrives. Before any model is
fit, the base rates of those labels need to be tabulated. A
classifier that predicts "no NFL outcome" for every player-season would be
correct more than 90 percent of the time, and so the model chosen needs to exceed this base rate.

This post measures how often each outcome happens, over the entire eligible population, and grounds the rates with examples. Four questions organize the results:

+ *Expecting the draft event to be rare, under five percent of eligible seasons*
+ *Expecting undrafted free-agent entry to rival the draft as an NFL route*
+ *Expecting the per-season chance of NFL entry to rise over a player's eligible seasons*
+ *Expecting entry prevalence to be roughly stable across draft classes*

Each question is stated as a claim the data can settle, and each is answered
with a table or figure backed by an assertion.

## 2. Data and terms

The unit of measurement, or observation, here is a **player-season**: one player's one college
season with a recorded stat line i.e. they played during the season. Rates are computed over **eligible
player-seasons**, seasons whose following draft the player could actually
have been selected in. A row is eligible when the draft arrives at least
three years after the player's high-school graduation, so a freshman season
is never an at-risk exposure or in other words, a season that is not eligible. Draft classes
whose outcomes may occur in the future are excluded rather than counted as misses.

Every eligible season ends in exactly one of the outcomes below.

```{r}
#| label: terms
terms <- tribble(
  ~Term                         , ~Meaning                                                                                                                                        ,
  "Drafted"                     , "Selected in the NFL draft held the spring after the season. Reported by round: round 1; rounds 2 to 3; rounds 4 to 7."                         ,
  "Undrafted free agent (UDFA)" , "Not selected in that draft, but on an NFL roster within the entry window afterward. Signed as a free agent, matched by a guarded name lookup." ,
  "NFL entry"                   , "Drafted OR signed as an undrafted free agent. The broadest 'made it' label."                                                                   ,
  "Made roster, rookie games"   , "Among players who entered: on an NFL regular-season roster in the entry year, and how many regular-season games they appeared in that year."   ,
  "Season status"               , "What the season turned out to be; the five possible statuses are defined in Section 3.2."
)
kable(terms, caption = "Table 1: the outcomes and terms used throughout")
```

A note on the uncertainty intervals: whenever a percentage is reported below, it comes
with a 95 percent confidence interval, the range the true rate plausibly
falls in given how many seasons were observed. When an event is rare, that
range is wide; a rate estimated from a few hundred seasons carries more
uncertainty than one estimated from tens of thousands. The interval style is
Wilson's, chosen because it behaves well for rare events like these.

```{r}
#| label: load
# The connection message is an implementation detail; the reader sees only
# the counts in the visible chunk below.
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfb2nfl.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
outcomes <- tbl(con, "outcomes") |> collect()
dbDisconnect(con)

risk <- outcomes |>
  filter(draft_eligible, outcome_observed_d) |>
  mutate(
    outcome_signed_udfa_d = coalesce(outcome_signed_udfa_d, FALSE),
    outcome_drafted_d = coalesce(outcome_drafted_d, FALSE),
    outcome_nfl_entry_d = coalesce(outcome_nfl_entry_d, FALSE)
  )

n_risk <- nrow(risk)
n_players <- n_distinct(risk$playerId)
```

```{r}
#| label: risk-set
risk_set <- tibble(
  Measure = c("Eligible player-seasons", "Distinct players"),
  Count = format(c(n_risk, n_players), big.mark = ",")
)
kable(risk_set, caption = "Table 2: the risk set")
```

```{r}
#| label: grain-guard
#| include: false
# The draft and UDFA events are mutually exclusive and their union is the
# entry label, on every row. A violation here would poison every rate below
# (a naive mean(na.rm = TRUE) over a partially NA flag once read UDFA
# prevalence at 35 percent instead of 4.7).
stopifnot(
  !any(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d),
  all(
    risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d ==
      (risk$outcome_drafted_d | risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d)
  )
)
```

A player usually contributes several eligible seasons, so the two counts in
Table 2 differ. Each event, however, lands on exactly one row per player:
the guards above and the player-level counts below both rely on that.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 How often each outcome occurs

*Expecting the draft event to be rare, under five percent of eligible
seasons.* ✅ **The expectation holds.** Deductively: out of every 100
eligible player-seasons, about 4 end with the player drafted and about 8 end
with the player reaching the NFL by any route.

```{r}
#| label: ledger
ledger <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    Outcome = c(
      "Drafted, any round",
      "  Drafted, round 1",
      "  Drafted, rounds 2 to 3",
      "  Drafted, rounds 4 to 7",
      "Signed as an undrafted free agent",
      "NFL entry (drafted or UDFA)"
    ),
    n_event = c(
      sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d),
      sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_draft_round_d == 1L),
      sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_draft_round_d %in% 2:3),
      sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d & risk$outcome_draft_round_d >= 4L),
      sum(risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d),
      sum(risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d)
    )
  )
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  transmute(
    Outcome,
    Events = format(n_event, big.mark = ","),
    `At risk` = format(n_risk, big.mark = ","),
    Prevalence = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_event / n_risk),
    `95% CI` = sprintf(
      "[%.1f%%, %.1f%%]",
      100 * wilson(n_event, n_risk)["lo"],
      100 * wilson(n_event, n_risk)["hi"]
    )
  )

kable(
  ledger,
  caption = "Table 3: how often each outcome occurs among eligible player-seasons"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: ledger-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(mean(risk$outcome_drafted_d) < 0.05)
```

To make the rows concrete: the first-round row is Joe Burrow in 2020, first
overall, and Cameron Ward in 2025, also first overall, two quarterbacks from
earlier posts in this series. The rounds 4 to 7 row is Jordan Travis,
selected 171st in 2024. The undrafted row is Shane Buechele, who signed with
Kansas City after the 2021 draft, and Kyle Allen, who signed with Carolina
after the 2018 draft. The routes differ in how they announce themselves, but
as routes into the league they are the same size: 4.7 percent of eligible
seasons end in a UDFA signing against 3.6 percent in a draft selection.

Among the `r format(sum(risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d), big.mark = ",")`
player-seasons that end in NFL entry, 56.6 percent arrive undrafted. For
every two players the draft announces, roughly three talk their way onto a
roster without hearing their name called.

### 3.2 What happens to a season: the five statuses

*Expecting exhausted eligibility to be the most common end-of-season status.*
❌ **The expectation does not hold.** Most eligible seasons simply continue:
the player comes back the next year.

Each eligible season ends in exactly one of five mutually exclusive statuses.
Four are defined by the player's own result; the fifth is defined by the
data's failure to observe a result.

```{r}
#| label: status-terms
status_terms <- tribble(
  ~Status               , ~Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              ,
  "continuing"          , "The player appears again on a roster in the next college season. The season is not an outcome, just another turn of the eligibility clock."                                                                                                                                                             ,
  "drafted"             , "The player is selected in the draft following this season. The same event also appears as the drafted label in Section 3.1."                                                                                                                                                                            ,
  "signed_udfa"         , "The player is not selected in that draft but appears on an NFL roster in the entry window afterward. The same event appears as the UDFA label in Section 3.1."                                                                                                                                          ,
  "exhausted_undrafted" , "This is the player's last observed college season, he was not drafted after it, and no NFL roster appearance follows. Eligibility ran out with no NFL outcome."                                                                                                                                         ,
  "left_data"           , "The player does not appear next season, but his roster record says a next season should exist: he left the data while still eligible to keep playing, through a transfer with sitting time, an injury retirement, or a departure the data cannot observe. A season ending here has an unknown outcome."
)
kable(status_terms, caption = "Table 4: the five end-of-season statuses")
```

```{r}
#| label: status
status_tab <- risk |>
  count(status_end_of_season, name = "seasons") |>
  mutate(
    share = seasons / sum(seasons),
    # Reader-facing labels for the statuses defined in Table 4, in the same
    # order as the factor levels below.
    status_label = dplyr::recode(
      status_end_of_season,
      "continuing" = "Still playing (continuing)",
      "exhausted_undrafted" = "Exhausted eligibility undrafted",
      "left_data" = "Left the data early",
      "signed_udfa" = "Signed as a UDFA",
      "drafted" = "Drafted"
    ),
    status_end_of_season = factor(
      status_end_of_season,
      levels = c(
        "continuing",
        "exhausted_undrafted",
        "left_data",
        "signed_udfa",
        "drafted"
      )
    )
  )

# Bars ordered by descending share, largest at top.
p_status <- ggplot(
  status_tab,
  aes(share, reorder(status_label, share))
) +
  geom_col_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = paste0(
        status_label,
        ": ",
        format(seasons, big.mark = ","),
        " (",
        scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1),
        ")"
      )
    ),
    width = 0.55,
    fill = "#1B9E77"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .05))
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl() +
  labs(x = "Share of eligible player-seasons", y = NULL)
girafe(ggobj = p_status, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 4)
```

```{r}
#| label: status-table
status_out <- status_tab |>
  transmute(
    `Season status` = status_label,
    Seasons = format(seasons, big.mark = ","),
    Share = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
kable(status_out, caption = "Table 5: how eligible seasons end")
```

```{r}
#| label: status-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  abs(sum(status_tab$share) - 1) < 1e-8,
  status_tab$share[status_tab$status_end_of_season == "continuing"] > 0.45,
  status_tab$share[status_tab$status_end_of_season == "exhausted_undrafted"] >
    0.3,
  status_tab$share[status_tab$status_end_of_season == "left_data"] > 0.05
)
```

The reason is the shape of the data rather than a surprise in it: a player
who reaches eligibility usually plays several eligible seasons, so most
eligible rows are mid-career, and a mid-career season ends with another
season coming. Exhausting eligibility undrafted is the most common *final*
destination, at 33.1 percent of eligible seasons. The `left_data` share is
7.6 percent, about one eligible season in thirteen: the player vanishes from
the data before the roster record says a next season should exist. A
transfer with sitting-out time or an injury retirement produces exactly this
pattern, and the modeling conventions treat those seasons deliberately
rather than as draft failures.

### 3.3 The per-season chance of entry

*Expecting the chance of NFL entry to rise over a player's eligible seasons.*
✅ **The expectation holds.** The measure is the discrete-time hazard: among
players still unentered and still playing after 1, 2, 3, ... eligible
seasons, the share whose very next draft is the one that takes them.
`eligible_season_index` counts those seasons from one. Think of it as
waiting in line at the draft: the first pass through the line is cheap, the
later ones are not.

```{r}
#| label: hazard
hazard <- risk |>
  group_by(eligible_season_index) |>
  summarise(
    seasons = n(),
    across(
      c(outcome_drafted_d, outcome_signed_udfa_d, outcome_nfl_entry_d),
      mean
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(seasons >= 100)

hazard_long <- hazard |>
  select(
    eligible_season_index,
    Drafted = outcome_drafted_d,
    `UDFA` = outcome_signed_udfa_d,
    `NFL entry` = outcome_nfl_entry_d
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-eligible_season_index, names_to = "outcome", values_to = "p")

p_hazard <- ggplot(
  filter(hazard_long, outcome != "NFL entry"),
  aes(eligible_season_index, p, color = outcome)
) +
  geom_line_interactive(linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point_interactive(size = 3) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(hazard_long, outcome == "NFL entry"),
    aes(eligible_season_index, p),
    linewidth = 1.4,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray35"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(hazard_long$eligible_season_index))) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  theme_cfb2nfl() +
  labs(
    x = "Eligible season index (1 = first season the player could be drafted)",
    y = "Event probability in that draft",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Dashed line: NFL entry (drafted or UDFA). Indices with <100 seasons omitted."
  )
girafe(ggobj = p_hazard, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: hazard-table
hazard_out <- hazard |>
  transmute(
    `Eligible season index` = eligible_season_index,
    Seasons = format(seasons, big.mark = ","),
    `Drafted` = scales::percent(outcome_drafted_d, accuracy = 0.1),
    `UDFA` = scales::percent(outcome_signed_udfa_d, accuracy = 0.1),
    `NFL entry` = scales::percent(outcome_nfl_entry_d, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
kable(hazard_out, caption = "Table 6: the per-season hazard of each outcome")
```

```{r}
#| label: hazard-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  all(diff(hazard$outcome_nfl_entry_d[1:4]) > 0),
  hazard$outcome_signed_udfa_d[4] > hazard$outcome_signed_udfa_d[1],
  hazard$outcome_drafted_d[3] > hazard$outcome_drafted_d[1]
)
```

The chance of entry climbs from 4.1 percent in a player's first eligible
season to 20.4 percent at the fourth, and the UDFA chance climbs even
faster, from 1.8 to 16.1 percent. Joe Burrow and Cameron Ward both sit where
the curve is steep: each was drafted first overall in his third eligible
season, where the entry chance is 17.6 percent and the drafted chance 5.7.
Jordan Travis waited one season longer, to the fourth eligible season, where
the chance is highest of all, and he heard his name in the fifth round. A
player still unentered by his third eligible season waits from a thinner
pool, and the models should see that through the index term rather than
treating every eligible season as exchangeable.

### 3.4 Trends across draft classes

*Expecting entry prevalence to be roughly stable across draft classes.*
❌ **The expectation does not hold, in one direction.** The rate of entry
drifts down over the years the data covers.

```{r}
#| label: trend
trend <- risk |>
  group_by(draft_year) |>
  summarise(
    seasons = n(),
    drafted_ev = sum(outcome_drafted_d),
    entry_ev = sum(outcome_nfl_entry_d),
    drafted = drafted_ev / seasons,
    entry = entry_ev / seasons,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    entry_lo = wilson(entry_ev, seasons)["lo"],
    entry_hi = wilson(entry_ev, seasons)["hi"]
  ) |>
  ungroup()

p_trend <- ggplot(trend, aes(draft_year)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = entry_lo, ymax = entry_hi),
    fill = "gray80",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(y = entry), linewidth = 1.4, color = "gray35") +
  geom_line(aes(y = drafted), linewidth = 1.4, color = "#1B9E77") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_cfb2nfl() +
  labs(
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Prevalence among eligible seasons",
    caption = "Gray: NFL entry with 95% interval band. Green: drafted."
  )
girafe(ggobj = p_trend, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: trend-table
trend_out <- trend |>
  transmute(
    `Draft class` = draft_year,
    `Eligible seasons` = format(seasons, big.mark = ","),
    `Drafted` = scales::percent(drafted, accuracy = 0.1),
    `NFL entry` = scales::percent(entry, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
kable(trend_out, caption = "Table 7: entry prevalence by draft class")
```

```{r}
#| label: trend-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  max(trend$drafted) > 0.05,
  min(trend$drafted) < 0.03,
  last(trend$entry) < first(trend$entry)
)
```

Entry prevalence falls from 8.9 percent in the 2012 class to 6.7 percent in
2025, and the drafted rate falls from 5.9 to 2.6 percent, while the UDFA
share of entry grows to compensate. Two forces plausibly combine, and both
are mundane: the stat-line population grows faster than the 253-pick draft,
so the same number of picks spreads over more eligible seasons, and NFL
roster coverage deepens over the years, so the guarded UDFA lookup catches
more of the signings that always happened. Either way, the class of 2025 is
not the class of 2012 with different players; it is a somewhat rarer
positive class.

### 3.5 Whether entrants play in their first NFL season

*Expecting most entrants to appear on an NFL roster in their entry year.*
✅ **The expectation holds.** Conditioning on the
`r format(sum(risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d), big.mark = ",")` players who
entered, the second-stage labels describe what arrival bought.

```{r}
#| label: entry-year
entry_first <- risk |>
  filter(outcome_nfl_entry_d) |>
  group_by(playerId) |>
  slice_min(draft_year, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE) |>
  ungroup()

entry_tab <- entry_first |>
  summarise(
    entrants = n(),
    made_roster = mean(outcome_made_roster_entry_year),
    zero_games = mean(outcome_rookie_games_entry_year == 0),
    median_games = median(outcome_rookie_games_entry_year),
    q75_games = quantile(outcome_rookie_games_entry_year, 0.75),
    q95_games = quantile(outcome_rookie_games_entry_year, 0.95)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    `Entrants` = format(entrants, big.mark = ","),
    `Made entry-year roster` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * made_roster),
    `Played zero rookie games` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * zero_games),
    `Median rookie games` = median_games,
    `75th percentile games` = q75_games,
    `95th percentile games` = q95_games
  )
kable(
  t(entry_tab),
  caption = "Table 8: the rookie season among players who entered the NFL"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: entry-guard
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  nrow(entry_first) ==
    sum(risk$outcome_drafted_d) + sum(risk$outcome_signed_udfa_d),
  # The named examples' facts above must not rot under a refresh.
  entry_first$outcome_rookie_games_entry_year[
    entry_first$player == "Cameron Ward"
  ] ==
    17L,
  entry_first$outcome_rookie_games_entry_year[
    entry_first$player == "Joe Burrow"
  ] ==
    10L,
  all(
    entry_first$outcome_rookie_games_entry_year[
      entry_first$player %in% c("Jordan Travis", "Shane Buechele")
    ] ==
      0L
  )
)
```

Nearly all entrants, 98.5 percent, appear on an entry-year NFL roster. That
figure is partly mechanical: the UDFA link is defined by roster presence, so
an undrafted entrant cannot fail the roster test by construction, and the
number should be read as a check on the link rather than as a finding. The
games column carries the real information. Cameron Ward, first overall,
played all 17 rookie-season games in 2025. Joe Burrow played 10 in his
injury-shortened 2020 season. The median entrant plays one game; 47.6
percent play none, Jordan Travis's and Shane Buechele's line, and Kyle
Allen's two games are closer to the middle of the distribution than his
roster spot suggests. Getting there and playing are separated by a wide
margin, which is why the pipeline carries the second-stage labels at all.

## 4. Summary

+ The draft event occurs in 3.6 percent of eligible player-seasons (95%
  interval 3.5 to 3.8), and the draft-plus-UDFA entry event in 8.3 percent.
+ The UDFA route exceeds the draft route: 3,239 signed seasons against 2,479
  drafted seasons, and 56.6 percent of all entrants arrive undrafted.
+ The per-season chance of entry rises from 4.1 percent at eligible season
  one to 20.4 percent at season four.
+ Entry prevalence drifted down across draft classes, from 8.9 percent
  (2012) to 6.7 percent (2025), with drafted prevalence falling by more than
  half.
+ Most eligible seasons (51.0 percent) end with the player continuing;
  33.1 percent end with exhausted eligibility undrafted, and 7.6 percent with
  the player leaving the data early.
+ Among entrants, the median rookie season is one game; 47.6 percent play
  none.

## 5. Discussion

The results point at three practical conclusions for the modeling work that
follows.

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**The base rate is not fixed.** Drafted prevalence halved across the data's
span while entry fell by a quarter. A model validated out-of-time is scored
against rarer positives than it trained on, so calibration curves and
precision at fixed recall say more across years than accuracy or raw
discrimination figures.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**Waiting time carries signal.** The chance of entry varies fourfold over
the eligible-season index, and the UDFA chance climbs faster than the
drafted chance. Modeling drafted status alone discards that structure, and
modeling entry without routes discards the competition between them.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**Entry and playing are different questions.** Half of entrants play zero
rookie games. The second-stage labels (made roster, rookie games) are a
separate prediction problem, not a footnote on the first.
:::

Two caveats bound the figures. The high-school graduation year is imputed
for players without a recruiting record, and the imputation mis-times
redshirts and junior-college transfers, shifting rows in and out of the
risk set. Cameron Ward is the textbook case: his clock is imputed from his
first stat season, yet he arrived by the junior-college route, so his true
wait was longer than the recorded one. And the `left_data` status is
informative censoring the pipeline flags but does not resolve. Neither
caveat is likely to move any prevalence by more than about a percentage
point, but both matter at the player level where the models operate.
